title: Insect Diversity
text:
Biological Diversity



Biological diversity - Variation of life on Earth

Present in all levels of biological organization

Two main dimensions:

Interspecific - Variation when comparing individuals of different species Ex. Femur length of a dog vs. a cat
Intraspecific - Variation when comparing individuals of the same species Ex. Claw size of two male crabs

title: Insect Diversity
text:
Why Does Diversity Matter?



Ecosystem function

Uphold species interactions, pollination, + carbon cycle

Ecosystem services

Water + agriculture

Ecosystem stability

If one species declines, others can fill it’s niche

All species are important, regardless of their usefulness to humans

title: Insect Diversity
text:
How Do We Measure Biodiversity?

Abundance - # individuals of a species in an area
Richness - # of different species in an area
Evenness - How common or rare a species is in an area

title: Insect Diversity
text:

3

3

title: Insect Diversity
text:
How Do We Measure Diversity

Shannon-Wiener Index

H’ - Index of species diversity
R - Species richness
pi - Proportion of R that species i makes up
Higher H’ = greater diversity

1. Hymenoptera



Ants, bees, wasps, sawflies
2 pairs of wings (hindwing/forewing)

Wings are connected by small hooks

Often have stinger/ovipositor
Characteristic “pinched waist”

title: Insect Diversity 2
text:
2. Lepidoptera



Moths and Butterflies
2 pairs of wings
Wings are covered in tiny hair-like scales

title: Insect Diversity 2
text:
3. Coleoptera



Beetles
2 Elytra and 1 pair of wings

Elytra - Hard wing coverings

title: Insect Diversity 2
text:
4. Diptera



Flies
One pair of wings and 1 pair of halteres

Halteres - Small little nubs that are located underneath the forewings, instead of HWs

Used for balance

title: Insect Diversity 2
text:
Data analysis

t-test - Compares the means of two sets of data to see if they are statistically different
Null Hypothesis - “There is NO effect of treatments”

Ex. High and low plant diversity treatments will NOT differ

p-value - Value of the likelihood that data supports the null hypothesis

if p > 0.05, null hypothesis is accepted. NOT statistically significant.
if p < 0.05, null hypothesis is rejected. Statistically significant.

Regression lines -Estimates relationship between dependent and independent variables
R2 - Measure of how well a model explains variation in the dependent variable

Does not compare REAL data, only modeled data
